reports.title: MONSTER BEVERAGE REPORTS 2026 THIRD QUARTER FINANCIAL RESULTS

desk.headline: Record sales up 16.7% to $2.56bn, ahead of estimates; margin slips on aluminium costs; no guidance given
results: Net sales reached a quarterly record of $2.56bn, up 16.7% (16.3% excluding currency moves), beating the $2.49bn estimate.
Sales outside the US jumped 28.1% to $1.20bn, now 47% of the total; Latin America rose 48.8%, led by Brazil.
Gross margin fell to 54.7% from 55.7% on higher aluminium can and freight costs, partly offset by price increases.
Heavier marketing and freight spending meant operating income grew only 6.4% to $718.7m; GAAP EPS rose 7.8% to $0.29 ($0.30 adjusted, which excludes a $19.9m Hawaii property write-down).
About $100m of shares were bought back in the quarter (2.3m shares at $43.87); about $800m of buyback capacity remains. Figures reflect the 2-for-1 share split of August.

guidance.summary: Monster gives no financial guidance, and the release has no outlook section. On the call management repeated that it does not guide, but said US price increases took effect on 1 November.

points: US price rises came in on 1 November, through list-price increases and/or smaller promotional allowances; management expects little effect on volumes.
Raw aluminium is up about 36% year on year and tariffs have pushed up the Midwest Premium; management expects can costs to keep edging up into at least Q1 2027.
October sales rose about 11.1% year on year despite one fewer selling day, and US category growth picked up again after a late-summer slowdown.
International growth was broad: Brazil up about 70%, China 43.8% and India 67.2%; in India a court granted interim relief over a ban on the 'energy drink' label.
Management named SNAP benefit changes and fuel prices as pressures on US consumers this year.
call.source: Call transcript: The Motley Fool, 6 Nov 2026; plus scanner-data presentation (Exhibit 99.2)

watch: Whether the 1 November US price increases hold volumes as management expects.
Aluminium and freight costs versus gross margin, which fell a full point this quarter.
Pace of international growth, especially Latin America, China and India.
